name: Myanmar
headline: Myanmar: −2.0% growth in 2025, 21.1% inflation, debt 52% of GDP
sections: Myanmar is a $82.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 87th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew −2.0% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $6,012 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 25.1% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 21.1% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, down from 27.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 9.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 52% of GDP (2025), a moderate level. The general government balance is −4.9% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +1.8% of GDP (2025). Net FDI inflows were 1.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 56% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 67.1 years (2024). Population: 54.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
